First, we find the derivative of $f(t)$ by differentiating each component.

$$
{f}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\sqrt{t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{1-2t})\,\,\,\, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2{t}^{6})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{t}} \\ -2{e}^{1-2t} \\ -12{t}^{5}\end{aligned}]
$$

Next, we calculate ${f}^{″}(t)$ by differentiating ${f}^{′}(t):$

$$
{f}^{″}(t)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{\sqrt{t}}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2{e}^{1-2t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-12{t}^{5})\,\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{{t}^{3/2}} \\ 4{e}^{1-2t} \\ -60{t}^{4}\end{aligned}]
$$
